instrumentIsNotSurfaceProbe: This artifact was NOT produced by scripts/surface-probe.mjs. Read at source 2026-09-19: that instrument's gate is scripts/enforcement/probe-close-gate.mjs, whose GATED_ROW (line 49) tests /^P-(\d+)$/ against GATED_RANGES -- OPS-23 rows P-151..P-174 and OPS-24 rows P-186..P-365. theRead.subject: GET /api/domains/business-licenses?cityKey=template-city
theRead.whyThisRoute: a real content read of a record-bearing domain through the product's own server, served to a minted fixture staff identity -- not a unit call into the new module. The probe reaches the gate the way a person does.
theRead.readerTenantIsNotThePackTenant: the reader is bastrop_tx and the pack read is template-city, deliberately: it makes the row's tenant (the reader's) provably different from the pack's city_key, which is the scoping clause.

predicates.acceptanceItem: pre-fix, show the absence (the falsifier for the whole row, and it must fail before the change)
predicates.measured: At ee9c5d5 the write path does not exist: 53 .mjs files under src/ searched with the design's own pattern (/(access_log|accessLog|audit_log|auditLog|recordRead|logRead|read_log|who_viewed)/), 0 matches, accessLogWritePath false. The SAME staff read is still SERVED -- HTTP 200, 17 records -- and the row counts are recorded as UNMEASURABLE, not 0, because at that ref there is no store to read (ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND on src/access-log.mjs). That is the pre-fix defect in one line: reads served, nothing written, an unanswerable 'who looked'.

predicates.acceptanceItem: a read by a named fixture staff identity writes exactly one record carrying who, which record, which lens and when
predicates.measured: post-fix at 3b56973: one row. who = sub 'fixture-staff-01'; whose reads = tenant 'bastrop_tx' (the READER's); which record = city_key 'template-city' + route '/api/domains/business-licenses' + record_id 'business-licenses'; which lens = lens_id 'development-services' (the DOMAIN's own lens, read off the record that was served); when = read_at '2026-09-19T00:52:22.037Z'. All four fields the row names, plus the two the scoping clause needs.

predicates.acceptanceItem: a second identity's read writes a second
predicates.measured: fixture-staff-02 (tenant some-other-city) read the same route and wrote its own row, id 2, tenant some-other-city. Two identities, two rows, neither overwriting or absorbing the other.

predicates.acceptanceItem: a tenant's reads never appear under another tenant (proved by violation)
predicates.measured: asked in both directions by the instrument: rows for tenant bastrop_tx that carry some-other-city's sub = 0; rows for tenant some-other-city that carry bastrop_tx's sub = 0; verdict 'scoped'. A scoping claim tested only by reading its own tenant has not been tested, which is why the instrument asks the other way too.

predicates.acceptanceItem: a forced log-write failure REFUSES the read rather than serving it, verified by violation
predicates.measured: forced through the environment, not through a mock: K_SERVICE set with DATABASE_URL unset is a deployment that has no durable store, so the write cannot happen. The read answered HTTP 503 with error 'access_log_write_failed', reason 'no_durable_store', refused true, servedRecords null, and no record content anywhere in the body; the row count was unchanged (1 before, 1 after). The read was NOT served. The plant was then removed and the same read was served again (200, 17 records), with the row count going 1 -> 2: the refusal was the missing store, not a broken route.

predicates.acceptanceItem: reads through the MCP surface are logged the same way
predicates.verdict: HELD -- declared in the row by amendment, reported not built
predicates.measured: Accounted for in the close under mcpSurface: the surface is hauska-mcp-server PR #70 (repo empressaioemail-tech/hauska-mcp-server), files src/dashboards-tools.ts + src/dashboards-client.ts, and the write would have to land at that client's read seam. NOT measured by this instrument because it is another repo and another card, which is what the dispatch says it is.

productTestSuite.theTwoFailuresAreInherited: dev-services-naming.test.mjs:202 (date arithmetic, off by one: [-41,11,199] where [-40,12,200] is expected -- a local-timezone artifact of expiryOffsetDays, not of this change) and server.test.mjs's G-132 people-and-access block (fetch failed / ECONNRESET). BOTH were reproduced at the base commit BEFORE being attributed: running src/server.test.mjs alone at ee9c5d5 gives 26 pass / 1 fail, and across two base runs the failing test DIFFERED (:1070 in one, :1105 in the other), which is the flake moving inside one block rather than a regression.

whatThisArtifactDoesNotProve: It does not measure the MCP surface. That clause is held by amendment and reported, not built -- see predicates[5].
It does not prove anything live. Both runs are local, against a server the probe starts itself; no deployed instance was read, and this lane is not a deploy.

It does not prove the log is durable in production. The post-fix runs exercise the memory store (no K_SERVICE, no DATABASE_URL). The deployment posture is exercised only in the direction the row demands of it: with no durable store, the write refuses and so does the read. A live Neon write is NOT claimed.
It does not prove Who looked can now be drawn. The board still refuses to render, by design, and redrawing it against this trail is a follow-on lane's work.
The v1 product (smartcity-os) is untouched and unmeasured here.
